name: Mechanical Cliff Notes
text: DAWN is a setting-agnostic, grid-based combat game using pools of d6s: 4+ is a Hit and each 6 is a Critical Hit that adds another die. Structured combat and unstructured play use mostly separate character features. Influence and Antagonism connect both modes. Characters build a custom Ability for unstructured play and combine individual Techniques rather than choosing a restrictive class. Ordinary equipment and inventory are handled through the fiction, not item accounting.

name: Inspirations And Assumptions
text: DAWN draws on battle shōnen, tactical games, and narrative TTRPGs. It assumes the group enjoys fictional combat, uses a world where defeat need not mean death, and communicates respectfully while sharing dramatic spotlight. Groups that do not share these assumptions should discuss changes before play and choose another game if they cannot reconcile them.

name: What DAWN Does Not Do
text: DAWN is not designed to evoke sustained horror, bypass major conflicts instead of confronting them, or model a fully fluid supernatural system where everyone freely learns the same broad powers. Its genre focus also does not attempt to reproduce every shōnen convention. These are design boundaries, not prohibitions, and groups may need substantial adaptation to work outside them.

name: World Creation Activity
text: Choose a rotating leader. They propose an answer; the group marks it Might Use or Won't Use, and any firm objection makes it Won't Use. Rotate left, repeating the prompt after a rejection or moving on after a possible acceptance. Decide: real-world period; source and publicity of the supernatural; public knowledge or concern; functional and aesthetic inspirations for empowered characters; their short name; how they help ordinary people; a natural enemy; the world's short name; and its factions and reasons to support or oppose them. A solo creator may instead try 3–4 ideas per prompt.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Rebellion
text: Show them what they did to you; make them pay. The world has rules, organizations, and traditions that preserve its status quo, but your existence breaks those rules. Why? Also ask whether and how the Change affected your rule-breaking nature.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Oath
text: Power requires discipline, and discipline requires focus. Something that happened to you made you take an Oath toward someone or something. What is it? Also ask to whom or what you made this Oath, and why.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Community
text: Not family and not coworkers, but something more special. After moving away from your family, you became deeply integrated into a second group. Who are they? Also ask whether this community is connected to the other player characters.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Disappearance
text: Something inside you is dead, and you have to move on. You once belonged to a rich community whose peers respected you and had your respect, but you can never go back. Why? Also ask whether that community still exists and how it fares without you.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Past
text: You used to be like them; how the years fly. Choose the Your Story question of any other Outlook and answer it in addition to this one. Also ask what has happened to you since then and how often you still think about those days.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Future
text: Everyone else is doing so well; begin the climb. Once, and only once before the adventure begins, you meet a legendary person whom you have heard about and idolized all your life. Who are they? Also ask how you resemble them and how you differ.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Fall
text: Everyone knows a fall can happen but never expects their own. Something supernatural implanted itself in you. What is it? Also ask how much you know about what happened and whether it relates to the Change that began this Series.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Rise
text: Imagine that some people live without luxury. Through extraordinary coincidence or fortune, you received a life-changing windfall. What was it? Also ask why you pursued the Opportunity instead of spending the rest of your days in opulence.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Comfort
text: Heroism is admirable, but small things keep us human. Choose a hobby or activity, unrelated to the adventure's main Change or Opportunity, in which you are deeply invested. Also ask whether going on the adventure helps you pursue it.

name: Primary Outlook Question: Your Weakness
text: If it is not true—if you are not the best—are you even yourself? Your life is full of people and achievements affirming your unmatched status, but once you faltered in that belief. Why? Also ask how many people know it happened and who they are.

name: Character Creation Checklist
text: Choose a concept and Tier. Assign Attributes, choose Outlooks and Boons, spend Ranks on Skills and an Ability, then buy Technique Levels. Finish by recording your derived statistics.

name: Starting Attributes
text: Assign 4, 3, 2, and 2 among the Attributes. Body represents physical health and strength and affects Health and physical power. Talent covers speed and stunts and affects Speed and physical power. Spirit covers supernatural instinct and affects Focus and magic. Mind covers mundane knowledge and rational thought and affects utility actions. A high Primary Attribute is usually more effective than spreading increases thinly. Attribute growth and the Technique-Level conversion are handled by the builder.

name: Starting Ranks
text: A new hero starts with 8 Character Ranks. Spend at least 4 on Skills; the rest may be spent on Skills or an Ability. Ranks range from 1 to 3.

name: Outlooks and Boons
text: Choose one Primary Outlook and two of its Boons. If that Outlook specifies an inherent Boon, take it in addition to those two. Boons apply only in unstructured play. As Tier increases, a hero may advance the Primary Outlook or branch into Secondary Outlooks, to a maximum of three total Outlooks: one Primary and up to two Secondary.

name: Technique Levels
text: A new hero has 5 Technique Levels. Buy Levels in order within a Technique. The searchable Technique catalogue contains the complete LionWing text for every Level.

name: Reading The Technique Catalogue
text: Every Technique has three Levels that must be taken in order. A hero may take Techniques from at most three Archetypes: the first is their Primary Archetype and the others are Secondary Archetypes. Complexity stars and tags describe intricacy and broad themes but have no mechanical effect. Flavor text is fiction and also has no mechanical effect. The six Archetypes are Powerhouse for sustained fights, Vagabond for defeating single targets, Bulwark for team defense, Altruist for helping allies, Disruptor for restriction and control, and Ruiner for high-impact, high-cost effects.

name: Ability Formula
text: Build an Ability from Verbs, Nouns, and Conditions. Its cost is calculated from the selected words and Rank. Symbol-specific exceptions are shown beside the Ability editor.

name: Derived Statistics
text: Health equals 10 + Body + twice Tier. Speed equals 2 + half Talent, rounded up; Focus equals 1 + half Spirit, rounded up. LionWing has no Guts statistic.

name: Story Question: Birth
text: Where and in what condition was your character born? A loving, close-knit community suggests Light and more detail about Family. Becoming an outcast from a healthy community suggests Accursed and asking why. Abandonment at a young age suggests Wolf and may skip the Family question.

name: Story Question: Family
text: Who shaped your character in childhood? Privilege, royalty, or a secret clan suggests Deceive or Command and Blessed or Loyal; ask whether they still belong. Hard-working or business family suggests Endure or Connect and Apprentice or Light; ask how the family is now and why the character left. Systemic or fundamental disadvantage suggests Move or Absorb and Rebel or Quiet; ask what the family could provide.

name: Story Question: Ambition
text: Why did your character leave their family, and what does the family think? Being pushed toward a goal suggests Loyal and whether the character truly wants it. Leaving to pursue a dream suggests Confident and who supports it. Being forced from home suggests Wolf and asking what they know about why it happened.

name: Story Question: Violence
text: How was the character trained to face violence, and when did they first face real danger? Circumstances that forced them to fight suggest Break or Menace and whether it made them stronger. Family training suggests Finesse or React and defining the tradition. An ambition that made them a better fighter suggests Luck or Tinker and asking how far they will go for the dream.

name: Story Question: Ability
text: What is the character's Ability, if any, and how did they first encounter other Abilities? A useful Ability suggests Blessed or Confident and asking when it was discovered. An Ability seen as harmful suggests Quiet or Accursed and asking what made it seem negative. Having no Ability yet suggests Rebel or Apprentice and asking how the character feels about that.

name: Story Question: Change
text: Discuss with at least the Narrator—and preferably the group—what suddenly changed in the world. Secret movements invite asking what the character knows compared with most people. A great success or failure by a nobody invites their opinion of that person. A sweeping change beyond mortal influence invites asking how it affected their personal life.

name: Optional Story Step: Settling Down
text: DAWN often begins during a character's rising action, but that is not required. If their personal journey has already peaked and entered a steady decline, record where they are now and let them follow the other characters as those characters rise.

name: Story Question: Opportunity
text: What recent opportunity to solve a practical problem or advance an ambition will bring the character to the other players? Coordinate with the Narrator if this opportunity appears in the first session. A natural event invites asking who else it affected; personal stakes invite asking how prepared the character is; joining an organization invites asking what they thought of it beforehand.

name: Example Hero: Qayid Āl-Rashid
text: Tier 1 Rebel. Attributes: Body 4, Talent 3, Spirit 2, Mind 2. Skills: Break +2, Endure +1, React +1, one custom Skill +0. Boons: Until My Last Breath; Overexertion. Ability—Gravity Well [1]: You Can Enhance Gravity So Long As You Touch The Target; a direct tool for debilitating opponents.

name: Example Hero: Yvon Chevalier
text: Tier 1 Quiet. Attributes: Body 2, Talent 4, Spirit 3, Mind 2. Skills: Lurk +2, Move +2, Intuit +1, Unveil +1. Boons: The Talent; Stalking Beast. Ability—Virtue: The Imaginary Number [1]: You Can Become Shadow; a cheap, mostly aesthetic Ability used for shadowy movement and stealth.

name: Example Hero: Titania, The Prodigy
text: Tier 1 Loyal. Attributes: Body 2, Talent 2, Spirit 3, Mind 4. Skills: Unveil +1, Tinker +1, Absorb +1, Luck +1. Boons: Fish Out Of Water; My Master's Teachings. Ability—Tonitru Companion [1]: You Can Launch Lightning If You See The Target; lightning stands in for electricity to keep the image magical.

name: Example Hero: Anseis Garrison
text: Tier 1 Confident. Attributes: Body 2, Talent 3, Spirit 2, Mind 4. Skills: Deceive +2, Move +1, Luck +1, one custom Skill +0. Boons: Chatty; Perspective Of A Lancer. Ability—Virtue: Insatiable Venus [1]: You Can Attract People So Long As You Hear It; a long-reaching pull with a very loose restriction.

name: Combat Recipe: Magical Brawler
text: Attributes: Body 4, Talent 2, Spirit 3, Mind 2. Start with SpellSword II. Choose an Elemental Affinity II: Flame Heart, Frost Veiler, Thunder Blood, or Wave Rider. Choose a Martial Art I: Martial Artist, Street Fighter, Technician, or Skirmisher. Tier-up paths: another Affinity; +2 Martial Art; +2 Rising Challenger; +2 Technician; or +1 SpellSword and +1 Berserker.

name: Combat Recipe: Scarred Warrior
text: Attributes: Body 4, Talent 3, Spirit 2, Mind 2. Choose a Fighting Style III: Dragonslayer, Street Fighter, Breacher, or Dual Wielder. Choose a Physical Build II: Speed Demon, Duelist, Vanguard Defender, Flagellant, or Mundane. Tier-up paths: +2 another Fighting Style; another Physical Build; +2 Skirmisher; +2 Feral Arcanist; or +2 Iron Bodied.

name: Combat Recipe: Tricksy Shinobi
text: Attributes: Body 2, Talent 4, Spirit 2, Mind 3. Choose a Signature Technique III: Chemist, Mind Breaker, Surgeon, Enchained, or SwarmKin. Choose a Subtle Weapon II: Martial Artist, Knife Juggler, Gunslinger, Dual Wielder, or Bloodletter. Tier-up paths: +2 another Signature Technique; another Subtle Weapon; +2 Street Fighter; +2 Cutpurse; or +2 Spellcrafter.

name: Combat Recipe: Death-Dealing Assassin
text: Attributes: Body 3, Talent 4, Spirit 2, Mind 2. Choose a Main Weapon III: Blade Master, Reaper, Sniper, Ranger (called Long Draw in this recipe), or Assassin. Choose a Method II: Intimidator, Untouchable, Cunning Fighter, Predator, or Analyst. Tier-up paths: +2 another Main Weapon; another Method; +2 Skirmisher; +2 Void Soul; or +2 Autophage.

name: Combat Recipe: Keen Caster
text: Attributes: Body 2, Talent 2, Spirit 4, Mind 3. Choose an Ability Type III: Flame Heart, Frost Veiler, Thunder Blood, Wave Rider, or Light Bender. Choose a Casting Type II: Spellcrafter, Bombardier, Eradicator, Ritualist, or Grim Ascendant. Tier-up paths: +2 another Ability Type; another Casting Type; +2 Dramaturge; +2 Zealot; or +2 Compassionate Sage.

name: Combat Recipe: Supportive Mage
text: Attributes: Body 2, Talent 3, Spirit 4, Mind 2. Choose an Arcane Blessing III: Compassionate Sage, Temporal Sage, Replicator, Deckbuilder, or Abjuring Sage. Choose a Bent II: Talisman Exorcist, Eradicator, Analyst, or Empath. Tier-up paths: +2 another Arcane Blessing; another Bent; +2 Will-O-Wisp; +2 Guard Caller; or +2 Spellcrafter.

name: Combat Recipe: Battlefield Maven
text: Attributes: Body 2, Talent 3, Spirit 2, Mind 4. Start with Cunning Fighter I. Choose Secret Knowledge II: Detective, Modified Meister, Battle Instructor, or Siren. Choose a Last Resort II: Martial Artist, Gunslinger, Dual Wielder, or Bloodletter. Tier-up paths: another Secret Knowledge; another Last Resort; +2 Skirmisher; +2 Cunning Fighter; or +2 Reflector.

name: Combat Recipe: Helpful Savant
text: Attributes: Body 2, Talent 2, Spirit 3, Mind 4. Choose a Special Interest III: Virtuoso, Fog Walker, Gourmand, Alchemist, or Will-O-Wisp. Choose a Personal Style II: Analyst, Dancer, Dramaturge, Empath, or Cutpurse. Tier-up paths: +2 another Special Interest; another Personal Style; +2 Skirmisher; +2 Iron Bodied; or +2 Tactical Master.
